report.source_text:
Frontal and frog-leg radiographs (Figure 1A, 1B) of the pelvis were ordered for assessment.
Radiographs revealed components of a healing right-sided ischial tuberosity avulsion fracture and a 5.8cm cluster of well-corticated, ovoid and crescent-shaped calcifications in the soft tissues near the ischial tuberosity and adjacent to the avulsed bone fragment. The affected ischial tuberosity displayed lucency and irregular margins.

report.source_text: The patient was expected to make a full recovery with conservative management including rest, physical therapy, and progressive return to activity. The patient’s right ischial tuberosity avulsion fracture improved clinically over several months and he was able to make a gradual return to his usual activities and sports.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 14-year-old boy presented with right hip pain after a fall with a popping sound two months prior. Clinical exam showed decreased strength with resisted knee flexion and tingling down the posterior thigh. Pelvic and hip X-rays revealed a healing right-sided ischial tuberosity avulsion fracture with lucency and irregular margins and adjacent soft tissue calcifications. MRI confirmed calcifications near the avulsed bone fragment. The patient was managed conservatively with rest, physical therapy, and gradual return to activity, with clinical improvement over several months.
